items.title: Fix HiRadix host cache load_back crash and internal-node eviction
items.body:
## Motivation

HiRadix host-cache load-back can crash when an evicted node is still treated as host-recoverable after its `host_value` has been freed by host eviction. In that state `load_back()` may call `len()` or `torch.cat()` on `None`, terminating the scheduler.

The same host eviction path also detached internal radix nodes when freeing host pages, which could orphan their child subtree even though the internal node was still needed as a prefix anchor.

## Modifications

- Protect every evicted node's host pages during `load_back()` and snapshot host segment lengths before restoring device pages.
- Add `TreeNode.storage_backed` to distinguish internal host nodes that can safely shed host pages because they are recoverable from L3 storage.
- Preserve radix subtrees when evicting host pages from storage-backed internal nodes; only true leaves are removed from the tree.
- Maintain storage-backed state on backup completion, L3 prefetch insertion, node split, storage clear, and backend detach.
- Stop host-prefix matching at the first host gap so descendant host pages are not counted as a contiguous loadable prefix.

Internal node host-page shedding does not emit `BlockRemoved(CPU)` because the block is not deleted from the radix tree; the subtree stays reachable and a host gap will trigger L3 recovery instead of router removal.

## Accuracy

The new tests cover host-evictable predicates, internal storage-backed host eviction, storage clear invalidation, host-gap matching, L3 prefetch insertion into storage-only nodes, duplicate host-page accounting after a host gap, and host protection during `load_back()`.

## Tests

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hiradix_cache.py python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py`

items.title: managers/detokenizer_manager: fix spurious eviction in LimitedCapacityDict when updating existing key
items.body:
## Motivation

`LimitedCapacityDict.__setitem__` unconditionally evicts the oldest entry
whenever `len(self) >= self.capacity`, even when the key being written
**already exists** in the dict. In that case the dict's size does not grow,
so no eviction should occur.

The result is a silent, premature loss of a live request's `DecodeStatus`.
When a key that is already present is overwritten:

1. `popitem(last=False)` ejects the oldest entry (a different, still-active
   request).
2. The updated key is re-inserted at the tail, corrupting insertion order.
3. The next genuinely new request then evicts what is now the *incorrectly
   promoted* oldest entry — one step earlier than it should be.

In the worst case this causes the `RuntimeError` / `KeyError` documented in
[#2812](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/2812) for requests that
are still actively generating tokens.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py`  
  Guard the eviction in `LimitedCapacityDict.__setitem__` with
  `key not in self`, so the oldest entry is only ejected when the insertion
  would genuinely grow the dict beyond capacity.

```diff
 def __setitem__(self, key, value):
-    if len(self) >= self.capacity:
+    if key not in self and len(self) >= self.capacity:
         # Remove the oldest element (first item in the dict)
         self.popitem(last=False)
     # Set the new item
     super().__setitem__(key, value)
```

The change is a single O(1) hash-map membership check with no effect on the
happy path (new keys at capacity).

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this change does not affect model forward passes or sampling
logic.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — the added `key not in self` check is O(1) and sits on the
detokenizer bookkeeping path, not the GPU-bound forward pass.

items.title: [SWA] Tighten chunk cache eviction guard to prevent premature slot freeing
items.body:
## Problem
The upstream SWA chunk cache eviction is firing too aggressively, freeing slots that are still within the active sliding window. This can cause KV cache correctness issues.

## Root Cause
The eviction condition `if new_swa_evicted_seqlen > req.swa_evicted_seqlen` commits to freeing for every small advancement of the eviction boundary, even when the active window hasn't fully moved past what we're freeing.

## Solution
Tighten the guard to `if new_swa_evicted_seqlen > req.swa_evicted_seqlen + sliding_window_size`. Only commit to an eviction when we've advanced the boundary by more than the sliding window size, ensuring nothing in the active window will be affected.

## Change
- **File:** `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`
- **Function:** `_evict_swa()`
- **Change:** Add guard condition checking `> evicted + sliding_window_size` instead of just `> evicted`

## Impact
- Fixes correctness issue where active KV cache slots could be freed prematurely
- Affects anyone using SWA models with chunk cache
- Low risk: only tightens the eviction invariant, doesn't change algorithm

items.title: Add WLFU radix cache eviction policy

## Motivation

This PR adds `wlfu` as a radix-cache eviction policy.

WLFU is an LRU variant with a frequency age penalty:

```python
priority = last_access_time - alpha * log1p(hit_count)
```

Since `RadixCache` evicts the smallest priority first, higher-hit nodes age out earlier than equally recent lower-hit nodes. This can reduce cache residency for prefixes that have already served many requests in finite shared-prefix workloads, leaving room for newer shared prefixes with upcoming reuse.

items.title: [1/N][HiCache PP]: use logical clock for deterministic LRU eviction across PP ranks
items.body:
Replace time.monotonic() with a logical batch-step counter for last_access_time in PP>1 mode. This makes both GPU and host eviction fully deterministic across PP ranks, preventing host-tree divergence that causes deadlocks and shape-mismatch crashes.

Problem: In PP mode, each rank calls match_prefix/insert independently, stamping nodes with wall-clock time.monotonic(). Micro-timing differences cause LRU priorities to diverge, so ranks evict different nodes, leading to host-tree inconsistency, prefetch shape mismatches, and deadlocks.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR adds a new radix cache eviction policy "seglen" (segment length) for hybrid models using MambaRadixCache.

Our approach is inspired by [Marconi prefix caching for hybrid LLMs](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.19379). Seglen heuristically approximates Marconi’s FLOPs-efficiency score, preserving the core idea of recomputation cost aware cache eviction while reducing implementation complexity of model-architecture specific FLOPs calculations.

Seglen ranks eviction candidates using replay length to the nearest reusable Mamba ancestor, combined with recency. Compared with pure LRU, this is intended to make eviction decisions more aware of recomputation cost for hybrid models.

```
sglang serve \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B \
  --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \
  --radix-eviction-policy seglen \
  --seglen-eff-weight 0.85
```

- Add seglen as a supported radix eviction policy for hybrid SSM models
- Implement seglen full-KV eviction and Mamba-state eviction in MambaRadixCache.

items.title: feat(eviction): add T-LRU (Tail-Optimized LRU) cache eviction policy
items.body:
## Motivation

Implement the **Tail-Optimized LRU (T-LRU)** cache eviction policy from [arXiv:2510.15152](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15152). Standard LRU evicts the least-recently-used KV cache block regardless of its impact on TTFT SLA. T-LRU improves SLA compliance by distinguishing:

- **TEL-safe blocks**: evicting them won't push the next turn's uncached token count above threshold `ξ` — these are evicted first.
- **Protected blocks**: evicting them would violate the SLA — these remain in standard LRU order.

A similar policy was recently merged into vLLM ([vllm-project/vllm#37825](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37825)). This PR is a SGLang-native adaptation.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/evict_policy.py`**
- Add `TLRUStrategy`: classifies each evictable leaf node as TEL-safe `(0, last_access_time)` or protected `(1, last_access_time)` using `B = max(0, L + Q̂ − ξ)` where `L = node.cumulative_tokens`.
- Add `get_cascade_priority()` to the base `EvictionStrategy` class (defaults to `get_priority`). `TLRUStrategy` overrides it to always return protected/LRU priority for **cascade nodes** — a SGLang-specific correctness fix (see below).

**`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py`**
- Add `cumulative_tokens` field to `TreeNode`, set on insert (`_insert_helper`) and split (`_split_node`).
- In `evict()`, use `get_cascade_priority()` when re-queuing a parent whose last child was just evicted.

**Correctness note — cascade eviction of shared prefix nodes:**
SGLang's radix tree shares prefixes across conversations. When all children of a shared prefix node are evicted, the parent becomes an evictable leaf. Its `cumulative_tokens` at that point equals its depth from root — not the full conversation history length `L` — which would incorrectly classify it as TEL-safe and allow it to jump ahead of protected conversation tails in the eviction order. The `get_cascade_priority()` override forces such nodes to protected/LRU priority. This issue does not arise in vLLM's per-request block model.

**`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/cache_init_params.py`** / **`python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`** / **`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`**
- Two new CLI args: `--tlru-xi-tokens` (SLA threshold in tokens) and `--tlru-qhat-tokens` (estimated next prompt length, default `200`).
- `--radix-eviction-policy tlru` activates the policy.

**`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_tlru.py`**
- Unit tests covering TEL-safe vs. protected classification, eviction ordering, cascade correctness, multi-turn prefix reuse, and end-to-end eviction with the real `RadixCache` + KV pool.

**Usage:**
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --radix-eviction-policy tlru \
  --tlru-xi-tokens 4096 \
  --tlru-qhat-tokens 200
```

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this PR adds a new eviction policy flag that is disabled by default (`--radix-eviction-policy lru` remains the default). No changes to model forward code or kernels.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — eviction runs off the hot path and the new policy is opt-in.

items.title: [Feature] Semantic eviction for radix cache
items.body:
## Motivation

Agent workflows often involve non-linear conversation patterns where context from previous turns becomes obsolete after summarization. Traditional KV cache management cannot efficiently handle these patterns, leading to:
- Unnecessary memory consumption from stale conversation history
- Reduced throughput due to memory pressure
- Inefficient cache utilization
- Lack of visibility into cache performance metrics

This PR implements **semantic-aware KV cache pruning** for SGLang's radix cache, enabling efficient handling of multi-round conversations with explicit semantic events (`start` and `reset`). Additionally, it adds comprehensive **KV cache metrics and monitoring** infrastructure to provide visibility into cache performance.

## Acknowledgments

This work builds upon foundational contributions from other community members:

- **@dougyster** (Doug Yang, Harvard): Initial KV cache endpoint infrastructure (`8210284a2`, `48cd09ff0`) that provided groundwork for KV cache monitoring.

## Modifications

### Part 1: Semantic-Aware KV Cache Pruning

#### Core Data Structures
- **`io_struct.py`**: Added `semantic_event` field to `GenerateReqInput` and `TokenizedGenerateReqInput`
- **`protocol.py`**: Added `semantic_event` field to OpenAI API request models

#### OpenAI API Endpoints
- **`serving_completions.py`**: Pass `semantic_event` to internal request
- **`serving_chat.py`**: Pass `semantic_event` to internal request

#### Tokenizer & Request Processing
- **`tokenizer_manager.py`**: Fixed `session_params` handling; Empty dict `{}` now creates `SessionParams()` instead of `None`

#### Scheduler & Session Management
- **`scheduler.py`**: Auto-create session when `semantic_event` provided; Pass `semantic_event` to `Req` object; Return `session_id` in response metadata

#### Scheduling Policy
- **`schedule_policy.py`**: 
  - Added `_prioritize_reset_requests()` method to prioritize reset requests in waiting queue
  - Modified `calc_priority()` to call prioritization at the beginning
  - Reset requests are processed before normal requests for faster memory cleanup

#### Output Processing
- **`scheduler_output_processor_mixin.py`**: 
  - Implemented **deferred batch pruning** with three phases:
    1. **Collect**: Gather all reset requests that finished in the batch
    2. **Unlock**: Release locks for all collected requests (decrement `lock_ref`)
    3. **Prune**: Perform pruning for all collected requests
  - Added semantic event handling in both prefill and decode batch processing
  - Eliminates race conditions where multiple reset requests share parent nodes

#### Radix Cache
- **`radix_cache.py`**: 
  - Added `prune_from_node()` method for semantic-aware pruning
  - Added `_node_exists()` method for safety checks
  - Added comprehensive safety checks:
    - Double-free protection (prevent pruning already-deleted nodes)
    - Root protection (prevent pruning root or its immediate children)
    - Child constraint checks (prevent pruning nodes with children)

### Part 2: KV Cache Metrics and Monitoring

#### Metrics Collection
- **`a4e22d249`**: Add KV cache slot utilization tracking and metrics
- **`724ba9b29`**: kvcache states as prometheus metrics
- **`a98047c34`**: kv cache logging metrics computation
- **`192b60d49`**: grafana label support

#### Infrastructure
- **`6ad408c51`**: Fix dev.Dockerfile: add setuptools and fix syntax error
- **`e5fdb20bf`**: Update sglang submodule URL to use forked repository

### Part 3: Documentation
- **`function_design.md`**: Comprehensive documentation of design, implementation, problems encountered, solutions, and performance impact

## Usage

### Backward Compatibility

**The usual pattern is fully preserved**. Existing applications continue to work without any changes:

```python
# Standard usage - no semantic_event needed
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="seed-oss-36b-instruct",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}
    ]
)
```

### Semantic-Aware Pruning

**Semantic events are only triggered when explicitly specified** in the request payload:

```python
# Start a new conversation session
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="seed-oss-36b-instruct",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Let's start a conversation"}
    ],
    extra_body={
        "semantic_event": "start"  # Auto-creates session
    }
)
session_id = response.extra_body.get("session_id")

# ... multiple conversation rounds ...

# Reset conversation after summarization
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="seed-oss-36b-instruct",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize our conversation"}
    ],
    extra_body={
        "semantic_event": "reset"  # Prunes old history
    }
)
```

### Session Management

Sessions can also be managed explicitly:


items.title: [Observability] Add KV cache eviction and load-back tracing
items.body:
## Motivation

Related to #13511 ([Roadmap] roadmap of request tracing) - "Tracing for uncovered engine components"

KV cache eviction (GPU→CPU) and load-back (CPU→GPU) are critical memory management operations in SGLang that directly impact request latency, especially under memory pressure. Currently, these operations are invisible in the existing OpenTelemetry tracing infrastructure, making it difficult to diagnose latency spikes caused by cache thrashing.

This PR adds trace events for both eviction and load-back operations, leveraging the existing `TraceReqContext.trace_event()` API with zero overhead when tracing is disabled.

## Modifications

### KV Cache Eviction Tracing (`common.py`)
- Added optional `trace_contexts` parameter to `evict_from_tree_cache()` and propagated it through `alloc_token_slots()`, `alloc_paged_token_slots_extend()`, and `alloc_paged_token_slots_decode()`
- When eviction actually occurs and tracing is enabled, records a `kv_cache_eviction` event with:
  - `num_tokens_requested`: tokens requested for allocation
  - `num_tokens_evicted`: tokens actually evicted
  - `duration_ms`: eviction duration in milliseconds

### Trace Context Collection (`common.py`)
- `alloc_for_extend()` and `alloc_for_decode()` now collect `TraceReqContext` from `batch.reqs` and pass them down to allocation functions

### Schedule Batch Integration (`schedule_batch.py`)
- `check_decode_mem()` and `release_req()` now collect trace contexts from `self.reqs` and pass them to `evict_from_tree_cache()`

### KV Cache Load-back Tracing (`schedule_policy.py`)
- Added `kv_cache_load_back` trace event around `init_load_back()` call in `_prefill_one_req_sliding_window()` with:
  - `host_hit_length`: number of tokens loaded back from host
  - `duration_ms`: load-back duration in milliseconds

items.title: [model-gateway] Implement Reactive Tree Eviction for Cache-Aware Policy
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->



## Motivation

Previously, the `CacheAwarePolicy` relied solely on a periodic background task to evict nodes from the approximate radix trees. This created a stability risk during traffic bursts: a surge of unique, long requests could cause the radix tree memory to grow unbounded between eviction cycles, potentially leading to **Out-of-Memory (OOM)** crashes.

This PR introduces a **"High-Water Mark"** approach, allowing the policy to trigger eviction immediately (reactively) when a worker's tree size exceeds a configurable threshold.

## Modifications

* **Core Policy Logic**: Modified `src/policies/cache_aware.rs` to include a `check_reactive_eviction` helper. This check is now called synchronously after every tree insertion in both balanced and imbalanced routing paths.
* **Configuration Extension**: Updated `CacheAwareConfig` in `src/policies/mod.rs` to include `enable_reactive_eviction` (bool) and `reactive_eviction_threshold` (f32).
* **Global Config & CLI**:
* Updated `PolicyConfig` enum in `src/config/types.rs`.
* Updated validation logic in `src/config/validation.rs` to ensure thresholds are .
* Exposed new parameters to the CLI in `src/main.rs`.


* **Language Bindings**: Updated Python bindings in `bindings/python/src/lib.rs` and CLI arguments in `bindings/python/src/sglang_router/router_args.py` to support the new safety features.
* **Test Utilities**: Updated `RouterConfig` builders in `tests/common/test_config.rs` and several integration tests to support the new configuration schema.

## Accuracy Tests

Added a comprehensive test suite in `tests/cache_aware_eviction_test.rs` which demonstrates:

1. **Vulnerability**: Without reactive eviction, a 2000-character burst into a 100-character budget results in 2000% memory usage.
2. **Protection**: With reactive eviction enabled, the same burst triggers an immediate synchronous cleanup, bringing the tree back to the safe limit (100 characters) before the request finishes.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

While synchronous eviction adds a small latency overhead to the specific request that triggers it, it significantly improves system **tail stability**.

* The check itself is a  lookup in the `tenant_char_count` map.
* By using a `reactive_eviction_threshold` (default 1.2x), we ensure that the expensive DFS eviction logic only runs when absolutely necessary to prevent OOM, rather than on every request once the limit is reached.

items.title: perf(speculative): eliminate device sync in EAGLE/ngram eviction
items.body:
## Summary

Remove boolean array indexing that causes GPU-CPU synchronization in the speculative decoding hot path. This addresses existing TODO comments in the codebase.

**Problem:** Boolean array indexing (`tensor[bool_mask]`) forces GPU-CPU device synchronization because the GPU must compute how many elements match before knowing the output size. This is a known performance anti-pattern in CUDA programming.

**Solution:** Replace boolean indexing with `torch.nonzero()` to get indices directly on GPU without synchronization.

### Changes

**eagle_info.py:**
- Line 443-446: Fixed `page_size == 1` branch eviction
- Line 460-463: Fixed `page_size > 1, topk == 1` branch eviction

**ngram_info.py:**
- Lines 209-214: Fixed `page_size == 1` branch eviction

### Before
```python
token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free(batch.out_cache_loc[evict_mask])
```

### After
```python
evict_indices = torch.nonzero(evict_mask, as_tuple=True)[0]
if evict_indices.numel() > 0:
    token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free(batch.out_cache_loc[evict_indices])
```

## Performance Impact

- Eliminates GPU-CPU sync points in speculative decoding hot path
- Expected 10-20% improvement in speculative decoding throughput
- Critical for high-throughput inference workloads

items.title: feat(EvictionStrategy): Add a new adaptive mixed cache eviction strategy to improving cache hit rate
items.body:
Add a new adaptive mixed cache eviction strategy called `AdapterMixStrategy`, which combines **hot/cold data separation** and **dynamic threshold adjustment** to fix the limitations of single LRU/LFU strategies, while improving cache hit rate and resource utilization.

**Limitations of Traditional Strategies:**
-**LRU Issue**: May evict frequently accessed cache data (due to overemphasizing recency over frequency).
-**LFU Issue**: May retain stale "zombie" high-frequency data (long-term unused but historically frequent) while evicting recently accessed items, leading to inefficient resource occupation.

### Initial Design
1. **Hot/Cold Data Separation**: Use a time threshold to split cache entries into two categories:
   - Hot data: Accessed recently;
   - Cold data: Not accessed for a long time.
2. **Differentiated Priority Sorting**:
   - Hot data: Sorted by "LFU (access count) + LRU (last access time)";
   - Cold data: Sorted by LRU;
   - Rule: Cold data is evicted first.

### Dynamic Threshold Adaptation (Simplifies Threshold Configuration)
To solve the problem that "time threshold requires manual configuration and is hard to evaluate", we designed a dynamic threshold adjustment logic:
- Adjust the time threshold based on the access ratio of hot/cold data to adapt to changing access patterns:
  - Shrink the threshold if there’s too much cold data (to classify more data as hot);
  - Expand the threshold if there’s too much hot data (to classify more data as cold);
- Default update interval: 60 seconds (to avoid frequent adjustments).

### Minimal Computational Overhead
1. Updates only once every 60 seconds—adds almost no extra computation;
2. Embeds the update logic into the existing `get_priority` method:
   - Users barely notice any changes;
   - No additional complexity for upper-layer code or callers.

### Benefits
- **Compared to LRU**: Prioritizes keeping frequently accessed data, reducing cases where "high-frequency data is mistakenly evicted";
- **Compared to LFU **: Eliminates "zombie high-frequency data" (data with high past access counts but no recent access) to avoid invalid cache occupying resources long-term;
 
With simple calculations, it fixes the drawbacks of single LRU/LFU strategies, while boosting cache hit rate and making better use of resources.
